name: Project FLAMING SWORD
purpose: Find every defect of the classes below in an unfamiliar codebase, queue them, fix what can be fixed mechanically in batches, prove each batch with the project's own test command, and land it — in one pass, with the decision trail written down.
why_it_exists: Every failure this estate paid for had the same shape: a document or a claim that was true once and drifted, and nobody re-running it. A human reviewer cannot re-run a hundred claims, and an agent will not unless told, so the sword exists to make the re-running the first step instead of the last.

defender.emit_when: before any change whose removal-of-something is the point (a test, a gate, a claim, a branch, a detector), and before any preservation work
defender.why: a change described only as 'fix X' cannot be told from a removal, because nothing stated what X defended; the frame states it first, so the cheapest satisfying output stops being a summary
rules: defends names an artefact that survives; an empty list is REFUSED, not defaulted
must_not_break names tests or paths, never 'don't break anything'
acceptance is a command plus an observable outcome; an adjective refuses the frame
control is a mutation that MUST be refused (RULE 0B-C); a second happy path is refused as a control
posture is mandatory for --preserve: whose copy, bytes_of_original (integer, must be 0), lawful_route, authority, what_must_not_be_carried

authority is one of the registered claims -- sony-v-connectix, sega-v-accolade, owner-holds-copy, eu-declined-to-legislate, us-exemption-declined, no-authority-claimed -- because an unverifiable authority is worse than none
a refused frame renders NO prompt, so nothing downstream can act on it
defender.default_landing: tools/sword.py --defend '<intent>' --target <artefact> [--preserve] (exit 1 when the frame is refused)

sentinel.why: the defender writes the frame; the sentinel refuses to let it be ACTED ON when its claims do not resolve -- a prompter can describe files that do not exist, tests that were never written and an evidence command nobody has, and the frame reads as rigour either way
sentinel.lands: SENTINEL OK / SENTINEL BLOCKED, exit 1; 12 controls

memory.why: a prompter that cannot ask what was learned re-learns the same defect every session, and one that imports the estate's memory libraries stops working on a machine that has none
adapters: jsonl (a lesson ledger, one object per line)
command (any command printing JSON lines -- this is how PMB/Engram/the board are reached without teaching this file their schemas)
memory.rule: an absent, failing or unparseable backend is UNMEMORED WITH ITS REASON, never 'no lessons found': the first is a fact about the run, the second is a fact about the world, and confusing them is the defect this whole project exists for
memory.writes: .flaming_sword/frames.jsonl (append-only; M-42's sweep requires a frame per queued id)

aio.what: user prompt -> frame -> sentinel -> memory -> ONE instruction object, or a refusal that renders NOTHING
aio.why: a model handed a prompt built on a hole fills the hole with prose; all three checks must pass before a prompt exists

defender.does_not_decide: whether the work is lawful; it refuses to frame work that has not said whose copy it is, which is the part a prompter can enforce

decision_blocks.emit_when: before any action that changes a file, a git config, a dependency or a service
decision_blocks.template:
DECISION  <one line>
  target:    <files/services touched>
  evidence:  <command run and what it printed>
  blast:     <what breaks if wrong, who notices>
  verify:    <command that proves it worked>
  rollback:  <how to undo>
decision_blocks.rule: evidence: none yet is legal once, for a read-only probe. It is illegal before a write.

decision_blocks.emit_when: before committing or pushing a batch
decision_blocks.template:
DECISION  land batch <n>
  batch:     <n> of <m>  (<ids>)
  test:      <command> -> <result>
  not_fixed: <items left open and why>
  rollback:  git revert <sha>
decision_blocks.rule: a land block with no test line is a claim, not a landing; not_fixed may be empty but may not be omitted

followups.shape: one sentence, hyper-edge, goal-oriented, names its target and the capability it unlocks; the last card is zero-shot reasoning and names its question, its evidence and its answer shape
forbidden: a chore the agent cannot do itself
followups.counting_rule: count them before sending; the mandate is 14 -- 13 hyper-edge cards, including the abyss card, then zero-shot reasoning LAST. 13 or 15 is a miscount, not a rounding

mandatory.prompt: Reason zero-shot from the evidence the previous thirteen cards produced: state the question, cite the evidence by path or command, answer in one pass with no worked example.
mandatory.why: the thirteen are evidence; the last card is the inference. A reasoning card with nothing behind it is a guess, which is why it is last

mandatory.prompt: Plan, build, verify and commit clean: take this tree to a green gate and a clean commit in one pass, then name what is still broken.
mandatory.why: planning, building, verifying and committing are one unit of work here; splitting them across a conversation is how a tree rots

mandatory.prompt: Take the sharpest capability jump available right now and land it.
mandatory.why: the rule asks for edge moves, not tidying; a set of fourteen chores satisfies the number and defeats it

hyper_edge_test: edge, not chore: names the capability, gate, measurement or proof that does not exist yet
one click does it: a complete prompt that names its target and outcome, never a plan
the agent owns it: nothing that has to be carried out by a human

supersedes.note: the baker's dozen predates the zero-shot reasoning card; the count was 12 before that

disposition.rule: every error is recorded as its own task the moment it is found, never at the end of the session
captured: a detector that could not run
a fix whose own detector still fires
a landing refused for any reason
a deletion housekeeping could not make
disposition.identity: stage + kind + subject, never the message: a count inside a message changes while the defect does not
disposition.repeat: a re-encounter increments seen and moves last_seen rather than adding a twin; a recurrence after a disposition is a NEW task

claims.rule: done / fixed / passes / verified / landed are claims and are worth what the command beside them is worth
claims.commit_requirement: a commit message that claims completion carries a line starting with `Verified:` naming the command and its result

stages.does: runs every detector, writes findings to .flaming_sword/findings.jsonl
stages.exit: 0 when the scan completed (even with findings); 1 when a detector could not run

stages.does: turns findings into an ordered queue (.flaming_sword/queue.jsonl), mechanical fixes first, then proposals
ordering: one item per file per batch unless the fix is the same edit

stages.does: applies the auto fixes of one batch, then re-runs the detectors affected by that batch
constraints: never fix an item the queue does not name
never widen a fix to a neighbouring defect
propose-only items are printed, never applied

stages.does: runs the project's own test command, then the detectors again
stages.rule: a fix whose detector still fires after the fix is a failed fix, whatever the test suite says

stages.does: one commit per verified batch, message naming the ids and carrying a Verified: line
stages.rollback: the batch id and the pre-batch sha are recorded before the commit
stages.constraint: no push. Landing is local by default; pushing is a separate, declared act.

stages.does: plans (and only with --apply, removes) what accumulated: bytecode and tool caches, editor leftovers, empty directories, disposable sweep state; reports unlanded batches and oversized untracked files as hazards a human decides on
stages.changes_nothing: by default -- dry run unless --apply is typed
refuses: any path git tracks, and the whole directory containing one
any symlink, and anything reached through one
anything that resolves outside the root
batches.jsonl: the landing record is history, not garbage
every non-cache deletion when git is unreadable, because content cannot then be told from by-product
stages.writes: .flaming_sword/housekeep.jsonl, one line per deletion, so 'what reclaimed the disk' has an answer tomorrow

stages.does: deep-dive web research for cutting-edge replacements, recorded as proposals, never auto-applied
stages.runs: before scan when the pass is a 'improve, do not just repair' sweep

detectors.detects: a path named inside a fenced code block that does not exist in the tree — the command a reader will copy and find missing
detectors.precision_note: fenced blocks only: a path in prose may be an example, a path in a block is an instruction
detectors.remedy: replace the reference with a command that exists, or delete the block

detectors.detects: the same watchlisted setting pinned to two different numeric values in two python files, in either form: `NAME = 0.89` or `os.environ.get("NAME", "0.89")` -- the env default is the canonical form here, and was invisible to this detector before 2026-11-01
detectors.precision_note: literal assignments only; a computed value is not a copy
detectors.remedy: pick the source, import it in the other file, and re-run whatever measured it

detectors.detects: a .githooks directory with no core.hooksPath pointing at it, so the tracked gates never run
documents whose fenced blocks run a bare `python -m pytest` while the same tree names an explicit interpreter path elsewhere
detectors.remedy: use the declared interpreter in the docs, or declare that the bare one is the target

detectors.detects: a CI workflow and a test suite that no workflow step runs
detectors.remedy: add the step, or delete the workflow — a green CI that runs nothing is worse than no CI

detectors.detects: a claims ledger whose declared command no longer produces the declared output
detectors.requires: claims.command in .flaming_sword/config.json; with no command this detector is UNRUN, not clean (fixed 2026-11-01, when it reported itself clean)
detectors.remedy: fix the page or the code; never delete the claim to make the run green

detectors.detects: a count in a document ('15 gates', '5,380 tests') with no command anywhere in the same section
detectors.precision_note: advisory: a figure may be a quotation. Reported so a human can decide, never auto-edited
detectors.remedy: cite the command, or drop the number

detectors.detects: missing required compliance elements (LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CI config, license headers) and optional elements (dependabot, CodeQL)
detectors.precision_note: configured via .flaming_sword/config.json compliance.required/optional; license-header checks Python files for copyright/license header
detectors.remedy: add the missing compliance files and license headers to source files

research.why_agent_executed: the runner has no network client and no API key; pretending to research would be the exact defect this project exists to find. The runner validates and queues what the agent records.
themes: the defect class itself (what the industry calls it, and how mature tools detect it)
the replacement technology for the component that keeps failing
the adjacent practice that removes the failure instead of detecting it

tiers.A: primary documentation, source, or a reproducible benchmark — adoptable
tiers.B: official index or changelog — identity only, not a capability claim
tiers.C: credible secondary write-up — adopt only when it matches an A source
tiers.D: blog, thread, snippet — a pointer, never a basis

adaptation_rules: adopt only what replaces a component this repo already has; a new component must remove one
no dependency without a licence check and a measured before/after on the same input
a proposed change that cannot name its verification command is not a proposal, it is a wish
tier D evidence never licenses a change to code that currently works

forbidden: deleting a claim, a gate or a test to make a run green
rebaselining a threshold without re-measuring it
editing a file outside the queue
reporting a detector as passing when it could not run

per_run: detectors that could not run (named, never counted as clean)
reporting.honesty_rule: a detector that could not run is UNRUN with its reason. UNRUN is not zero findings.
